title: Variables & Syscalls
description: Linux x86-64 ELF64, NASM Intel syntax, immediate values and syscalls
theory:
### Program shape on Linux x86-64

Every standalone program in this track is assembled to a **64-bit ELF relocatable**
(`nasm -f elf64`) and linked into an executable. When you use a global `_start` label
and talk to the kernel yourself, the **dynamic linker is optional** and `ld` is enough.
When you call **`extern`** symbols from the C library, you normally link with **`gcc`**
so startup files, libc, and ABI details are wired correctly.

Immediate values and register moves are your first “variables”: they are ephemeral,
but they are how you satisfy the Linux syscall calling convention. For **64-bit Linux**
syscalls, you place the syscall number in **`rax`**, arguments in **`rdi`**, **`rsi`**,
**`rdx`**, **`r10`**, **`r8`**, **`r9`**, then execute **`syscall`**.

### Exit and write syscalls

`sys_exit` (`rax = 60`) terminates the process; **`rdi`** carries the exit status.
`sys_write` (`rax = 1`) copies bytes from userspace to a file descriptor: **`rdi`**
is the fd (1 for stdout), **`rsi`** points at the first byte, **`rdx`** is the length.
Keep addresses of buffers in `.data` or `.bss` so they stay valid for the whole run.

```nasm
; Minimal exit(0)
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60         ; sys_exit
    xor rdi, rdi        ; status 0
    syscall

; Write "Hi" to stdout then exit — pattern used everywhere in this course
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H', 'i'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, len
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
```

### Assemble and link

Typical commands from the repo root mirror the exercise harness: assemble to `*.o`,
then `ld` for pure-syscall binaries or `gcc` when you import libc helpers. If you mix
hand-written `_start` with libc, pay attention to stack alignment and the AMD64 ABI
before calling C functions.

exercises.title: Exit cleanly
exercises.description: Write a program with global `_start` that exits with status 0 using the exit syscall. It should print nothing.
exercises.starter_code:
; NASM Intel, Linux x86-64
; Exit with code 0 (no output)

global _start
section .text
_start:
    ; rax = 60 (sys_exit), rdi = 0
    ; syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Write to stdout
exercises.description: Use the `write` syscall to print exactly `Hi` (two characters, no newline).
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H','i'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    ; rax=1 write, rdi=1 stdout, rsi=msg, rdx=len
    ; then exit 0
hints: After write, exit with `mov rax, 60` / `xor rdi, rdi` / `syscall`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H', 'i'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, len
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Call libc printf
exercises.description: Use **`extern printf`**, **`global main`**, and link with **gcc** (the runner detects `extern`). Print one line: `Hello from libc` followed by a newline. Expected stdout after trim is `Hello from libc` (the newline is trimmed).
exercises.starter_code:
default rel
extern printf
section .text
global main
main:
    ; align stack, then call printf with format in rdi
    ret
section .data
    fmt: db "Hello from libc", 10, 0
hints: `sub rsp, 8` before `call` helps satisfy 16-byte stack alignment on entry
`xor eax, eax` before `call printf` (AL = 0 vector regs for variadic)
exercises.solution:
default rel
extern printf
section .text
global main
main:
    sub rsp, 8
    lea rdi, [rel fmt]
    xor eax, eax
    call printf
    add rsp, 8
    xor eax, eax
    ret
section .data
fmt: db "Hello from libc", 10, 0

exercises.title: Three-byte write
exercises.description: Print exactly `Asm` (three letters, no newline) with a single `write` syscall from a `.data` buffer, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'A','s','m'
    mlen equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    ; rax=1 write stdout rsi=msg rdx=mlen then sys_exit 0
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'A', 's', 'm'
    mlen equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel msg]
    mov rdx, mlen
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
